events.title: The Botanical Series: The Reserve
events.description: The Botanical Series: The Reserve Thursday, October 8, 2026 from 6 to 8 p.m. Blue Ridge Court at The North Carolina Arboretum An elevated evening. A distinct Arboretum experience. The North Carolina Arboretum and Chemist Spirits have come together to create a one-of-a-kind botanical vodka inspired by the plants and landscapes of Western North Carolina. Developed through months of collaboration, the spirit features botanicals thoughtfully harvested from the Arboretum and transformed by Chemist Spirits into a distinctive expression of place. The Reserve offers an intimate opportunity to experience that collaboration at its most refined. Set against the mountain backdrop of Blue Ridge Court, this limited-capacity evening pairs botanical spirits, food and live music with a curated tasting experience led by Chemist Spirits. Explore the flavors and botanicals behind the spirit before creating your own botanical-infused cocktail, guided by the experts who developed it. Then settle in and enjoy the evening with live music and heavy hors d’oeuvres in one of the Arboretum’s most beautiful settings. Each guest will also receive a commemorative 40th Anniversary Arboretum tasting glass to take home. Parking is included. Please note: This event is for guests ages 21 and older. A valid photo ID will be required for age verification upon arrival. Learn more and purchase tickets here.

events.title: River Systems Field Class
events.description: River Systems Field Class with Anton DuMars Friday, October 23 | 11am – 5pm BRN – Core Register Here! For the River Systems Field Experience, we will observe processes and indicators along the Davidson River, a Blue Ridge tributary of the French Broad catchment basin. We consider channel hierarchy (first order, second order, etc.). Our stops include observation and discussions of flow and flood indicators and river forms, such as cut banks, point bars, and flood channels. We observe sediment texture, sediment load, and consider sediment source. This program provides transportation to and from the class location using our minibus. We will meet at the Arboretum and return to the Arboretum. If you prefer to meet us there, let us know and we will tell you where to meet. This program will take place outside and will follow easy to moderate trails. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. Anton DuMars , a resident of Black Mountain, NC, is an adjunct professor at the College of Charleston. His geological interests include fluvial, deltaic, and coastal processes. Ideally, he’s spending time on a hiking trail or aboard his sailboat. ● Members: Remember to enter your promo code upon checkout to receive your 10% member discount!
